Administration and Management::Accountin.domain_definition: Tax advisory helps people and organisations understand and follow tax law. Tax advisors and compliance officers interpret legislation, inspect tax returns and study financial statements, while auditors, budget analysts and financial controllers check that accounts are accurate. Accounting firms, government revenue agencies and large companies employ most practitioners, and chartered qualifications are required to practise.

Corporate finance and investment banking deal with how companies raise, invest and manage money. Securities and mergers analysts study company performance and financial statements, while controllers, budget analysts and bank managers oversee funds and financial processes. Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Accounting is the recording, checking and reporting of an organisation's money. Accountants prepare and interpret financial statements, audit records, advise on tax, control budgets, and handle billing, payroll and back-office processing. They work in accounting firms, banks, government agencies and businesses of all sizes; in Nigeria the chartered route runs through bodies such as ICAN or ANAN.

Trading is the buying and selling of financial assets such as currencies, shares, commodities and energy. Traders deal on markets throughout the day, securities analysts study market trends and financial products, and investment managers and planners advise clients on funds and risk. Banks, investment firms and brokerages are the typical employers.

Investment analysis is the study of companies, markets and financial products to decide where money should be placed. Analysts examine businesses and market trends, investment managers run funds and portfolios, financial planners advise clients, and traders buy and sell shares, currencies and securities. Banks, investment firms, insurance companies and pension organisations are the main employers.

Economics studies how money, markets and government policy shape a society. Economists and researchers analyse statistics and market trends, while advisers and policy analysts guide decisions on tax, trade and economic development, often working closely with local representatives. Government ministries, research bodies and banks are common employers.

Insurance protects people and businesses against loss in exchange for regular payments. Underwriters assess risk and price cover, claims handlers and managers settle claims, brokers arrange policies for clients, fraud investigators check suspicious cases, and some specialists run pension schemes. Insurance companies and brokerages employ most of the profession.

Credit analysis is the work of judging whether borrowers can repay what they owe. Credit analysts and advisers examine financial statements, analyse loans and assess borrower risk, while credit managers and mortgage brokers arrange and oversee lending. Banks and other lending institutions employ most people in this field.

Payroll and bookkeeping is the careful recording of an organisation's money, including wages, taxes, sales and payments. Clerks maintain records of financial transactions, prepare staff salaries, process insurance and tax paperwork, and support auditors and back-office operations using office software. Banks, insurance companies and businesses of every size employ them.

Keeping money safe and lending it out is the everyday business of banking and credit. Bank tellers and cashiers serve customers, credit analysts and advisers assess loans and mortgages, clerks handle settlements and foreign exchange records, and managers lead branches and credit unions. Banks, mortgage firms and credit unions are the natural workplaces.

Actuarial science uses mathematics and statistics to measure risk, mainly for insurance and pensions. Actuaries model how likely future events are and what cover should cost, underwriters and rating analysts assess individual risks, and claims handlers process what policyholders are owed. Most work in insurance companies, consulting firms and banks, and full actuaries qualify through professional fellowship examinations.

General management is the running of organisations and their departments. Managers direct budgets, finance, quality and facilities, consultants advise on strategy and business improvements, and senior executives and entrepreneurs lead whole organisations. Because every sector needs this work, managers are found in banks, factories, retailers, government agencies and non-profit organisations alike.

Public administration is the running of government and public institutions. Civil registration officers, urban planners and policy officers develop policy and public programmes, inspectors enforce customs, tax and safety rules, and senior officials and ambassadors lead ministries and diplomacy. Nearly all work in government ministries, agencies, local councils and embassies.

Compliance and regulation work makes sure people and organisations follow laws, rules and government policy. Officers inspect goods and borders, enforce tax and safety rules, shape public policy and programmes, and manage contracts, procurement and regulatory affairs inside organisations. Government agencies, banks and large companies employ most of them.

Project management is the planning and coordination of work so it finishes on time and within budget. Coordinators organise projects, procurement and office operations, senior managers lead programmes and departmental strategy, and analysts study processes to drive agile and lean improvements, often working with spreadsheets and business analysis. Construction firms, banks, government agencies and charities all need these skills.

Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

Urban mobility and smart city planning organise how people and transport move around cities. Transport planners and engineers design road, rail and airport projects, while land planners and smart city consultants apply urban planning and environmental policy to make cities work better. Government agencies, engineering firms and construction companies carry out this work.

Banks, mortgage firms and credit unions are the natural workplaces.

Telecommunications is the engineering behind phone calls, internet connections and data networks. Engineers design radio-frequency and signal systems, planners work out how much network capacity is needed, technicians install and maintain equipment, and managers direct projects, budgets and technical teams. Telecoms companies and government agencies are the usual employers, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Sales is the business of getting goods and services to buyers. Some practitioners purchase, broker and trade goods and commodities, others sell machinery, energy and technical products to businesses, manage key customer accounts, or serve shoppers on the shop floor, while directors set commercial strategy. Retailers, wholesalers, manufacturers and trading companies employ them.

Logistics deals with the practical movement of goods and people by road, rail, air and sea. Some workers drive buses, trucks and forklifts; others load and dispatch goods in warehouses and docks, manage fleets and ports, or coordinate shipping, customs and forwarding. Transport companies, warehouses, ports and event organisers are typical employers.

Travel and tourism serves people on the move for holidays, business and leisure. Travel consultants plan trips and sell tickets, tour organisers and park guides lead visitors around attractions, and stewards look after passengers on flights, ships and trains. Airlines, travel agencies, hotels, parks and tour companies are the common employers.

Hospitality is the service of looking after guests in hotels, restaurants and tourism. Receptionists and concierges welcome visitors, chefs lead kitchens, waiters and guides serve guests directly, and managers run hotels, events and tour operations while handling budgets and complaints. Hotels, restaurants, resorts and event companies provide the work.

Compliance and regulation work makes sure people and organisations follow laws, rules and government policy. Officers inspect goods and borders, enforce tax and safety rules, shape public policy and programmes, and manage contracts, procurement and regulatory affairs inside organisations. Government agencies, banks and large companies employ most of them.

Occupational health and safety focuses on preventing accidents, illness and harmful conditions at work. Inspectors visit factories, building sites, food businesses and hospitals to check that health, hygiene and waste laws are being followed, carrying out audits and reporting hazards. Many are employed by government agencies, with others working for large industrial and transport companies.

They typically work in technology firms, banks, telecoms companies and government agencies.

Cloud architects plan these systems, engineers build and program them, administrators keep networks and data centres running, and specialists monitor security and compliance. Common employers are technology firms, banks, telecoms companies and data centres.

Administration and Management::Informati.domain_definition: Insurance protects people and businesses against loss in exchange for regular payments. Underwriters assess risk and price cover, claims handlers and managers settle claims, brokers arrange policies for clients, fraud investigators check suspicious cases, and some specialists run pension schemes. Insurance companies and brokerages employ most of the profession.

Trading is the buying and selling of financial assets such as currencies, shares, commodities and energy. Traders deal on markets throughout the day, securities analysts study market trends and financial products, and investment managers and planners advise clients on funds and risk. Banks, investment firms and brokerages are the typical employers.

Actuarial science uses mathematics and statistics to measure risk, mainly for insurance and pensions. Actuaries model how likely future events are and what cover should cost, underwriters and rating analysts assess individual risks, and claims handlers process what policyholders are owed. Most work in insurance companies, consulting firms and banks, and full actuaries qualify through professional fellowship examinations.

Quantitative finance applies mathematics, statistics and economics to financial markets. Some practitioners buy and sell shares, currencies and other assets as traders; others analyse investments, risk and market trends to guide decisions; a third group builds the mathematical models behind pricing and risk. They usually work in banks, investment firms, insurance companies and trading houses.

Investment analysis is the study of companies, markets and financial products to decide where money should be placed. Analysts examine businesses and market trends, investment managers run funds and portfolios, financial planners advise clients, and traders buy and sell shares, currencies and securities. Banks, investment firms, insurance companies and pension organisations are the main employers.

Economics studies how money, markets and government policy shape a society. Economists and researchers analyse statistics and market trends, while advisers and policy analysts guide decisions on tax, trade and economic development, often working closely with local representatives. Government ministries, research bodies and banks are common employers.

Corporate finance and investment banking deal with how companies raise, invest and manage money. Securities and mergers analysts study company performance and financial statements, while controllers, budget analysts and bank managers oversee funds and financial processes. Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Keeping money safe and lending it out is the everyday business of banking and credit. Bank tellers and cashiers serve customers, credit analysts and advisers assess loans and mortgages, clerks handle settlements and foreign exchange records, and managers lead branches and credit unions. Banks, mortgage firms and credit unions are the natural workplaces.

Payroll and bookkeeping is the careful recording of an organisation's money, including wages, taxes, sales and payments. Clerks maintain records of financial transactions, prepare staff salaries, process insurance and tax paperwork, and support auditors and back-office operations using office software. Banks, insurance companies and businesses of every size employ them.

Telecommunications is the engineering behind phone calls, internet connections and data networks. Engineers design radio-frequency and signal systems, planners work out how much network capacity is needed, technicians install and maintain equipment, and managers direct projects, budgets and technical teams. Telecoms companies and government agencies are the usual employers, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Business intelligence turns an organisation's records into information that managers can act on. Teams include engineers and architects who build analytics systems, analysts and consultants who study business processes and recommend improvements, and mathematicians and statisticians who build quantitative models from the numbers. Such roles exist in banks, telecoms companies, retailers and large organisations of every kind.

Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Real estate is the business of land, buildings and property. Property managers look after buildings and tenants, brokers and investors arrange sales and purchases, and mortgage advisors and conveyancers handle finance, legal transfer and property financial analysis. Estate firms, banks and property companies are the typical workplaces.

FinTech engineering builds the software that powers financial services such as payments, banking apps and blockchain systems. Developers write backend code, data engineers manage the information flowing through these systems, and testers run structured checks, record faults and document results so money-handling software works reliably. Banks, payment companies and technology firms employ these teams.

General management is the running of organisations and their departments. Managers direct budgets, finance, quality and facilities, consultants advise on strategy and business improvements, and senior executives and entrepreneurs lead whole organisations. Because every sector needs this work, managers are found in banks, factories, retailers, government agencies and non-profit organisations alike.

Credit analysis is the work of judging whether borrowers can repay what they owe. Credit analysts and advisers examine financial statements, analyse loans and assess borrower risk, while credit managers and mortgage brokers arrange and oversee lending. Banks and other lending institutions employ most people in this field.

Accounting is the recording, checking and reporting of an organisation's money. Accountants prepare and interpret financial statements, audit records, advise on tax, control budgets, and handle billing, payroll and back-office processing. They work in accounting firms, banks, government agencies and businesses of all sizes; in Nigeria the chartered route runs through bodies such as ICAN or ANAN.

Tax advisory helps people and organisations understand and follow tax law. Tax advisors and compliance officers interpret legislation, inspect tax returns and study financial statements, while auditors, budget analysts and financial controllers check that accounts are accurate. Accounting firms, government revenue agencies and large companies employ most practitioners, and chartered qualifications are required to practise.

Compliance and regulation work makes sure people and organisations follow laws, rules and government policy. Officers inspect goods and borders, enforce tax and safety rules, shape public policy and programmes, and manage contracts, procurement and regulatory affairs inside organisations. Government agencies, banks and large companies employ most of them.

Legal practice covers the making, interpretation and application of law. Lawyers and legal consultants advise clients and argue cases, judges and court clerks run court processes and enforce decisions, and legal assistants compile documents and carry out legal research. Typical workplaces include law firms, courts, companies and government agencies.

Trading is the buying and selling of financial assets such as currencies, shares, commodities and energy. Traders deal on markets throughout the day, securities analysts study market trends and financial products, and investment managers and planners advise clients on funds and risk. Banks, investment firms and brokerages are the typical employers.

Economics studies how money, markets and government policy shape a society. Economists and researchers analyse statistics and market trends, while advisers and policy analysts guide decisions on tax, trade and economic development, often working closely with local representatives. Government ministries, research bodies and banks are common employers.

Investment analysis is the study of companies, markets and financial products to decide where money should be placed. Analysts examine businesses and market trends, investment managers run funds and portfolios, financial planners advise clients, and traders buy and sell shares, currencies and securities. Banks, investment firms, insurance companies and pension organisations are the main employers.

Accounting is the recording, checking and reporting of an organisation's money. Accountants prepare and interpret financial statements, audit records, advise on tax, control budgets, and handle billing, payroll and back-office processing. They work in accounting firms, banks, government agencies and businesses of all sizes; in Nigeria the chartered route runs through bodies such as ICAN or ANAN.

Keeping money safe and lending it out is the everyday business of banking and credit. Bank tellers and cashiers serve customers, credit analysts and advisers assess loans and mortgages, clerks handle settlements and foreign exchange records, and managers lead branches and credit unions. Banks, mortgage firms and credit unions are the natural workplaces.

Credit analysis is the work of judging whether borrowers can repay what they owe. Credit analysts and advisers examine financial statements, analyse loans and assess borrower risk, while credit managers and mortgage brokers arrange and oversee lending. Banks and other lending institutions employ most people in this field.

Insurance protects people and businesses against loss in exchange for regular payments. Underwriters assess risk and price cover, claims handlers and managers settle claims, brokers arrange policies for clients, fraud investigators check suspicious cases, and some specialists run pension schemes. Insurance companies and brokerages employ most of the profession.

Diplomacy and international relations manage a country's dealings with other nations. Diplomats and ambassadors lead embassies and represent their nation abroad, while political affairs and intelligence officers handle foreign policy, trade, election observation and humanitarian issues. Ministries of foreign affairs, embassies and international organisations are the typical employers.

Actuarial science uses mathematics and statistics to measure risk, mainly for insurance and pensions. Actuaries model how likely future events are and what cover should cost, underwriters and rating analysts assess individual risks, and claims handlers process what policyholders are owed. Most work in insurance companies, consulting firms and banks, and full actuaries qualify through professional fellowship examinations.

FinTech engineering builds the software that powers financial services such as payments, banking apps and blockchain systems. Developers write backend code, data engineers manage the information flowing through these systems, and testers run structured checks, record faults and document results so money-handling software works reliably. Banks, payment companies and technology firms employ these teams.

Legal practice covers the making, interpretation and application of law. Lawyers and legal consultants advise clients and argue cases, judges and court clerks run court processes and enforce decisions, and legal assistants compile documents and carry out legal research. Typical workplaces include law firms, courts, companies and government agencies.

Recruitment and employment services match people to jobs. Recruitment consultants, talent acquisition specialists and employment agents advertise vacancies, interview and select candidates, follow labour legislation and keep candidate information confidential, while employer branding specialists present organisations attractively to job seekers. Recruitment agencies and company human resources departments are the typical employers.

Compliance and regulation work makes sure people and organisations follow laws, rules and government policy. Officers inspect goods and borders, enforce tax and safety rules, shape public policy and programmes, and manage contracts, procurement and regulatory affairs inside organisations. Government agencies, banks and large companies employ most of them.

Some workers drive buses, trucks and forklifts; others load and dispatch goods in warehouses and docks, manage fleets and ports, or coordinate shipping, customs and forwarding. Transport companies, warehouses, ports and event organisers are typical employers.

Instructors give practical lessons in cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles and even vessels, follow a set curriculum, guard each student's safety and explain the rules of the road. Most work for driving schools accredited by the road safety authorities or run their own.

General management is the running of organisations and their departments. Managers direct budgets, finance, quality and facilities, consultants advise on strategy and business improvements, and senior executives and entrepreneurs lead whole organisations. Because every sector needs this work, managers are found in banks, factories, retailers, government agencies and non-profit organisations alike.

Telecommunications is the engineering behind phone calls, internet connections and data networks. Engineers design radio-frequency and signal systems, planners work out how much network capacity is needed, technicians install and maintain equipment, and managers direct projects, budgets and technical teams. Telecoms companies and government agencies are the usual employers, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Product management is the work of guiding a product from idea to finished item and setting the direction a business takes with it. Product owners and development managers lead strategy, engineers and architects build the underlying technology, and analysts scope requirements, costs and processes. Most work in manufacturing companies, technology firms and other large businesses.

Corporate finance and investment banking deal with how companies raise, invest and manage money. Securities and mergers analysts study company performance and financial statements, while controllers, budget analysts and bank managers oversee funds and financial processes. Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Urban mobility and smart city planning organise how people and transport move around cities. Transport planners and engineers design road, rail and airport projects, while land planners and smart city consultants apply urban planning and environmental policy to make cities work better. Government agencies, engineering firms and construction companies carry out this work.

Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

Supply chain management is about moving goods from where they are made to where they are needed, at the right time and cost. People in this field schedule freight, ships, rail and cargo movements, run warehouses and distribution, handle customs and sourcing, and analyse logistics costs. Employers include shipping lines, airlines, ports, manufacturers and trading companies.

Travel and tourism serves people on the move for holidays, business and leisure. Travel consultants plan trips and sell tickets, tour organisers and park guides lead visitors around attractions, and stewards look after passengers on flights, ships and trains. Airlines, travel agencies, hotels, parks and tour companies are the common employers.

Basic Medical Sciences::Human Anatomy::D.domain_definition: Biomedical science studies living things, from microbes to the human body, mainly through laboratory work. Microbiologists, pharmacologists and physiologists research organisms, medicines and how bodies function, while technicians run laboratory tests and support biology and agricultural science. Hospitals, research institutes, universities and pharmaceutical companies employ them; medical laboratory scientists in Nigeria are licensed by MLSCN.

Biomedical engineering combines engineering with biology and medicine to design equipment and materials used in healthcare. Biomedical engineers and biomaterials scientists develop and test medical devices, while research and robotics engineers work on new technologies for the body. They are employed by hospitals, medical device manufacturers and research laboratories.

Neuroscience and cognitive science investigate the brain, thought and behaviour. One side of the field involves scientists studying how the brain and mind work; the other involves psychologists and psychotherapists who assess and treat mental and behavioural health. They work in hospitals, clinics, schools and universities.

Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Bioinformatics and computational biology use computers and data analysis to study living things, from microbes to human genes. Scientists such as geneticists, microbiologists and bioinformatics specialists run laboratory experiments, analyse biological data and write scientific papers. They generally work in research institutes, universities and hospitals.

Forensic science applies science and computing to the investigation of crime. Digital forensics experts and security specialists recover evidence from computers and respond to cyber attacks, laboratory technicians run biological analyses, detectives gather evidence, and pathologists examine medical evidence. Employers include police services, government agencies and security firms.

Medical laboratory technology is the testing of blood and other body samples to help doctors diagnose and treat illness. Phlebotomists collect blood, while technologists and technicians run clinical chemistry and molecular tests, classify blood types, maintain laboratory equipment and keep patient records. Hospitals, clinics and diagnostic laboratories employ most practitioners.

Medicine is the profession of diagnosing and treating illness. General practitioners and specialist doctors examine patients and decide on treatment, technical staff provide laboratory, audiology and prosthetic support, and managers run hospitals and clinical information systems. Hospitals, clinics and government health agencies are the main workplaces, and doctors in Nigeria must register with the Medical and Dental Council.

Practitioners write and debug code, analyse what a program should do, test software at different levels, and manage changes to systems, in roles such as software analyst, tester, mobile application developer and cloud engineer. They typically work in technology firms, banks, telecoms companies and government agencies.

Sciences::Industrial Mathematics::D012.domain_definition: FinTech engineering builds the software that powers financial services such as payments, banking apps and blockchain systems. Developers write backend code, data engineers manage the information flowing through these systems, and testers run structured checks, record faults and document results so money-handling software works reliably. Banks, payment companies and technology firms employ these teams.

Sciences::Industrial Mathematics::D003.domain_definition: Artificial intelligence covers building computer systems that learn from data to recognise images, understand language and make predictions. Machine learning engineers, data scientists and researchers write computer programs, apply statistics, run computer simulations and train models, then present their results visually. Typical workplaces include technology companies, research institutes, banks and universities.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D050.domain_definition: Industrial automation focuses on the machines and control systems that run modern factories. PLC programmers and automation engineers design automated machinery, instrumentation technicians keep control systems working, and assemblers and supervisors build equipment and run automated production lines. Manufacturing plants and engineering firms are the usual employers.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D016.domain_definition: Electrical engineering deals with electricity, circuits and electronic devices. Engineers design power systems, batteries, sensors and electronics for products ranging from medical devices to satellites, while technicians test, calibrate and maintain electrical equipment and lines. Power companies, manufacturers, telecoms companies and construction firms employ them, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D132.domain_definition: Space science and exploration studies space and builds the craft that travel there. Aerospace and satellite systems engineers design spacecraft, flight and mission controllers monitor missions, and physicists, astrophysicists and astrobiologists carry out research using tools such as spectroscopy. Space agencies, research institutes and universities are the usual employers.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D140.domain_definition: Robotics engineering designs machines that sense, move and act with little human control. Robotics, automation and controls engineers develop the mechanical parts, control systems and software that make robots work, relying on technical drawings and mathematics. They typically work for manufacturing companies, engineering firms and research organisations.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D141.domain_definition: Quantum computing builds a new kind of computer based on the physics of atoms and light. Some specialists write quantum software, algorithms and cryptography, while others engineer the hardware, sensors and devices that run them. Work in this field is usually found in research laboratories, universities and technology companies.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D093.domain_definition: Electrical installation is the fitting and repair of wiring and electrical equipment in buildings, vehicles and industry. Electricians read wiring plans, install cables and equipment, inspect electrical supplies and resolve faults in homes, factories and vehicles. They work for construction firms, electricity companies and maintenance contractors, and contracting work in Nigeria requires a statutory licence.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D019.domain_definition: Renewable energy engineering produces electricity from sources such as sunlight, water and wind. Engineers design solar, wind and battery generation systems, operators run power plants and transmission networks, and technicians install and maintain power lines and solar equipment under strict electrical safety rules. Power companies, utilities and engineering firms are the usual employers.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D155.domain_definition: Nanotechnology and advanced materials involve studying and building substances at extremely small scales to give them new properties. Chemists, materials scientists and nanofabrication technicians run experiments, analyse chemical substances, make tiny components and write up their findings in technical papers. Research laboratories, universities and manufacturing companies are the usual employers.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D008.domain_definition: Telecommunications is the engineering behind phone calls, internet connections and data networks. Engineers design radio-frequency and signal systems, planners work out how much network capacity is needed, technicians install and maintain equipment, and managers direct projects, budgets and technical teams. Telecoms companies and government agencies are the usual employers, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D006.domain_definition: The Internet of Things connects everyday devices such as sensors, meters and appliances to the internet so they can send and receive information. Specialists write the firmware inside these devices, design the networks that link them, plan complete solutions, secure them against attack, and test that everything works, documenting any faults. Manufacturers, telecoms companies and technology firms are typical employers.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics

Sciences::Industrial Physics::D059.domain_definition: Space technology concerns the design and operation of spacecraft and satellites. Aerospace, avionics and satellite systems engineers design and test flight hardware, propulsion engineers work on spacecraft engines, and mission operations engineers run missions once craft are in orbit, drawing heavily on physics. Space agencies, aerospace companies and research organisations are the usual employers.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to Electric Circuits and Electronics

Sciences::Marine Science::D134.domain_definition: Naval architecture and marine engineering is the design of ships and the running of their machinery. Naval architects design and survey vessels and offshore energy installations, while marine engineers operate and maintain ship engines and systems at sea, from assistant to chief engineer. Shipyards, shipping companies and offshore energy firms are typical employers.

Sciences::Marine Science::D041.domain_definition: Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Sciences::Marine Science::D072.domain_definition: Geospatial science involves measuring, mapping and studying the Earth's land, water and minerals. Surveyors take precise measurements of land, mines and seabeds for maps and property records, while geologists, hydrologists and oceanographers study rocks, groundwater and the sea using mathematics and geographic information systems. Typical employers include mining companies, construction firms and government agencies.

Sciences::Marine Science::D144.domain_definition: Climate science and meteorology study the weather and the long-term behaviour of the atmosphere. Forecasters and meteorologists use instruments and specialised computer models to predict weather conditions, while climatologists, hydrologists and oceanographers analyse climate, water and ocean patterns. Typical employers are government weather agencies, aviation organisations and research institutes.

Sciences::Marine Science::D020.domain_definition: Environmental engineering tackles pollution, waste and water quality. Technicians operate water, wastewater and waste treatment plants, engineers design solutions to pollution, climate and sustainability problems, and inspectors check that organisations comply with environmental, health and safety laws. Water utilities, waste management companies, mining firms and government agencies employ people in this field.

Sciences::Marine Science::D142.domain_definition: Bioinformatics and computational biology use computers and data analysis to study living things, from microbes to human genes. Scientists such as geneticists, microbiologists and bioinformatics specialists run laboratory experiments, analyse biological data and write scientific papers. They generally work in research institutes, universities and hospitals.

Sciences::Marine Science::D120.domain_definition: Fisheries and aquaculture covers catching fish and farming aquatic stock. Managers run hatcheries and fish farms, technicians monitor fish health and mortality, and workers harvest stock, dive, moor cages and crew fishing boats, all within biosecurity and fisheries law. Fish farms, hatcheries and fishing companies are the main employers.

Officers navigate and command vessels, deckhands and engine crew keep ships running, naval engineers design ships and marine structures, and divers work underwater on construction, harvesting and rescue. Shipping companies, ports, fishing fleets and offshore firms provide most of the work.

Some workers drive buses, trucks and forklifts; others load and dispatch goods in warehouses and docks, manage fleets and ports, or coordinate shipping, customs and forwarding. Transport companies, warehouses, ports and event organisers are typical employers.

Sciences::Mathematics::D014.domain_definition: Actuarial science uses mathematics and statistics to measure risk, mainly for insurance and pensions. Actuaries model how likely future events are and what cover should cost, underwriters and rating analysts assess individual risks, and claims handlers process what policyholders are owed. Most work in insurance companies, consulting firms and banks, and full actuaries qualify through professional fellowship examinations.

Sciences::Mathematics::D002.domain_definition: Data engineering focuses on building the systems that collect, store and move an organisation's information. People in the field design data warehouses, connect databases to other software, write queries, and plan how information is structured so others can use it. Employers include banks, telecoms companies, technology firms and any large organisation that keeps substantial records.

Sciences::Mathematics::D009.domain_definition: Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

Power stations, hospitals, research institutes and regulators employ them.

Sciences::Medical Physics::D123.domain_definition: Radiography and medical imaging uses X-rays, CT, MRI, ultrasound and related technology to see inside the body and to treat disease with radiation. Radiographers and imaging technologists position patients and operate scanners, sonographers perform ultrasound examinations, and radiation therapists deliver radiotherapy. They work mainly in hospitals and diagnostic imaging centres.

Sciences::Medical Physics::D137.domain_definition: Medical physics and radiation therapy apply the science of radiation to diagnosing and treating illness, particularly cancer. Radiation therapists deliver treatment to patients, radiographers capture medical images, and medical physicists plan doses and keep equipment safe and accurate. People in this field work mainly in hospitals and cancer treatment centres.

Civil registration officers, urban planners and policy officers develop policy and public programmes, inspectors enforce customs, tax and safety rules, and senior officials and ambassadors lead ministries and diplomacy. Nearly all work in government ministries, agencies, local councils and embassies.

Social Sciences::Social Work::D143.domain_definition: Forensic science applies science and computing to the investigation of crime. Digital forensics experts and security specialists recover evidence from computers and respond to cyber attacks, laboratory technicians run biological analyses, detectives gather evidence, and pathologists examine medical evidence. Employers include police services, government agencies and security firms.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D078.domain_definition: Social sciences study how people, societies and institutions behave and change over time. Researchers such as sociologists, historians, criminologists and archaeologists design studies, gather and analyse data, and write academic papers and policy reports, often using statistics. They commonly work in universities, research institutes and government agencies.

course_anchors.title: Methods of Social Research and Statistics

Social Sciences::Sociology::D063.domain_definition: Economics studies how money, markets and government policy shape a society. Economists and researchers analyse statistics and market trends, while advisers and policy analysts guide decisions on tax, trade and economic development, often working closely with local representatives. Government ministries, research bodies and banks are common employers.

course_anchors.title: Introduction to African Societies and Culture
Methods of Social Research and Statistics

Social Sciences::Sociology::D151.domain_definition: Criminology and criminal justice cover the study of crime and the running of the justice system. Police officers and detectives investigate offences and handle evidence, prison officers guard and manage correctional facilities, and criminologists study why crime happens and supervise offender rehabilitation. Police services, prisons and government agencies are the main employers.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D046.domain_definition: Social work supports people facing difficulty, from children in care to families in crisis. Qualified social workers and counsellors guide individuals through problems such as family planning and recovery from violence, frontline workers support vulnerable adults and children in residential settings, and nannies and day-care workers mind children. Employers include government social services, care homes, charities and schools.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D073.domain_definition: Library and archive work is about organising, preserving and sharing information, records and cultural collections. Librarians and information managers help people find the material they need, curators plan exhibitions, and conservators and art handlers care for artefacts and digitise documents. Most posts are in libraries, museums, universities and government archives.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D037.domain_definition: Legal practice covers the making, interpretation and application of law. Lawyers and legal consultants advise clients and argue cases, judges and court clerks run court processes and enforce decisions, and legal assistants compile documents and carry out legal research. Typical workplaces include law firms, courts, companies and government agencies.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D009.domain_definition: Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

course_anchors.title: Methods of Social Research and Statistics

Social Sciences::Sociology::D064.domain_definition: Psychology and counselling deal with how people think, feel and behave, and with helping them through personal difficulty. Educational and health psychologists assess and support clients, while counsellors work with problems such as addiction, marriage and family planning, using client-centred methods. Hospitals, schools, social service agencies and private practices are typical settings.

Social Sciences::Sociology::D045.domain_definition: Public administration is the running of government and public institutions. Civil registration officers, urban planners and policy officers develop policy and public programmes, inspectors enforce customs, tax and safety rules, and senior officials and ambassadors lead ministries and diplomacy. Nearly all work in government ministries, agencies, local councils and embassies.

Veterinary Medicine::Veterinary Medicine.domain_definition: Veterinary science is the study and treatment of animal health and welfare. Veterinarians diagnose, treat and rehabilitate sick or injured animals, veterinary nurses assist with care and breeding procedures, and others provide animal therapy or study behaviour and nutrition. Practitioners work in veterinary clinics, on farms and for government agencies, and must register with the Veterinary Council of Nigeria to practise.

Animal care and grooming is the everyday looking after of animals, from feeding and cleaning to training and grooming. Attendants and kennel workers care for animals in shelters and boarding facilities, trainers teach dogs and horses, breeders raise animals, and groomers keep coats healthy and tidy. Kennels, stables, zoos and grooming salons are the typical workplaces.

Livestock, poultry and dairy work is the rearing of animals for food and other products. Farmers and breeders raise cattle, poultry, sheep, horses and bees and run dairy farms, while livestock workers feed, handle and groom animals under animal-welfare rules. Work is based on farms, ranches and dairies.

course_anchors.title: Poultry and Fish Production and Management

Veterinary Medicine::Veterinary Medicine.domain_definition: Bioinformatics and computational biology use computers and data analysis to study living things, from microbes to human genes. Scientists such as geneticists, microbiologists and bioinformatics specialists run laboratory experiments, analyse biological data and write scientific papers. They generally work in research institutes, universities and hospitals.

Neuroscience and cognitive science investigate the brain, thought and behaviour. One side of the field involves scientists studying how the brain and mind work; the other involves psychologists and psychotherapists who assess and treat mental and behavioural health. They work in hospitals, clinics, schools and universities.

Biomedical science studies living things, from microbes to the human body, mainly through laboratory work. Microbiologists, pharmacologists and physiologists research organisms, medicines and how bodies function, while technicians run laboratory tests and support biology and agricultural science. Hospitals, research institutes, universities and pharmaceutical companies employ them; medical laboratory scientists in Nigeria are licensed by MLSCN.

Biomedical engineering combines engineering with biology and medicine to design equipment and materials used in healthcare. Biomedical engineers and biomaterials scientists develop and test medical devices, while research and robotics engineers work on new technologies for the body. They are employed by hospitals, medical device manufacturers and research laboratories.

Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Public health protects the health of whole communities rather than one patient at a time. Inspectors enforce food, workplace and community health standards, officers and physicians coordinate emergency responses and prevention work, and scientists track diseases and analyse health statistics. Government agencies, hospitals and international health organisations are typical employers.

Radiography and medical imaging uses X-rays, CT, MRI, ultrasound and related technology to see inside the body and to treat disease with radiation. Radiographers and imaging technologists position patients and operate scanners, sonographers perform ultrasound examinations, and radiation therapists deliver radiotherapy. They work mainly in hospitals and diagnostic imaging centres.

Occupational health and safety focuses on preventing accidents, illness and harmful conditions at work. Inspectors visit factories, building sites, food businesses and hospitals to check that health, hygiene and waste laws are being followed, carrying out audits and reporting hazards. Many are employed by government agencies, with others working for large industrial and transport companies.

From crops to livestock, agricultural science combines farming practice with the study of plants, animals and the environment. Crop production managers, breeders and shepherds grow crops and raise animals, researchers study genetics, biology and aquaculture, and technicians supervise farm and fish sites. Farms, research institutes, agribusinesses and government agricultural agencies offer most positions.

Veterinary Medicine::Veterinary Medicine.domain_definition: Medicine is the profession of diagnosing and treating illness. General practitioners and specialist doctors examine patients and decide on treatment, technical staff provide laboratory, audiology and prosthetic support, and managers run hospitals and clinical information systems. Hospitals, clinics and government health agencies are the main workplaces, and doctors in Nigeria must register with the Medical and Dental Council.
